name: tax-inclusive-input
title: Tax-Inclusive Input
description: Price field with an explicit includes/excludes-tax toggle, a net + tax = gross readback, and flags for an "excludes" price that divides back to a round number, a mode switch that silently changed the total, and a typo'd rate like 0.18 or 180.

meta.stops: GST added twice to a price
meta.summary: Makes "includes / excludes GST" an explicit choice and reads back net + tax = gross, so tax isn't added twice.
catches: An "excludes tax" price that looks already taxed (divides back to a round number)
Switching mode that changed the total, with keep-the-total fix
Rates typed as a fraction (0.18), multiplier (1.18) or slipped digit (180)
limits: Default rate list is India's main GST slabs (0, 5, 18, 40); special rates (e.g. 3% on gold, 0.25%) and tobacco still on old rates are not included
Rounds to the currency's minor unit; invoice rounding rules may differ
Does not decide which rate applies to an item
a11y: Visible <label> on the amount; readback via aria-describedby
Rate input has an aria-label; includes/excludes is a radiogroup
Warnings and fixes in a polite live region

sources.label: PIB – GST rate rationalisation (56th GST Council), effective 22 Sep 2025

rules.note: Re-checked 2026-10-17 against PIB release 2164586 (8 Sep 2025): the 56th GST Council moved GST from four slabs (5/12/18/28%) to two main rates, 5% (merit) and 18% (standard), plus a 40% special rate for sin/luxury goods, effective 22 Sep 2025. The default list [0, 5, 18, 40] (0 = nil-rated) matches; special rates such as 3% on gold and 0.25% on rough diamonds, and tobacco items still on 28% plus cess, are not in it. Informational; check CBIC rate notifications for an item's rate.
